title: Playing Flying Home for Hampton and respecting the boss
summary: Cobb says he started Flying Home in Houston, that Hampton let him play as long as he liked, and that he never disrespected Hampton the way Jacquet did.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: But what did you do with Flying Home? Did you say that the -- you had a row with Illinois on -- about the way Illinois was playing Flying Home?

He told Illinois, you know, Hamp has a thing saying one more (inaudible) one more. So he was going to cut Illinois off, and he wasn't ready to go. But what Illinois did, he disrespected his leader, just (inaudible) him and turned around and (inaudible) you don't tell me when to cut off, and went back to blowing his horn, and Hamp brought the band in on D flat strain. And Illinois sat out there and played it.

So when he disrespected him and Gladys saw what happened, you know how Gladys is. She said, we don't need him. We don't need anybody to go buck you. You the boss. And they gave him his notice, and then that's when he called Chicago. But see, I didn't know all this then.
(Inaudible) you started to play Flying Home, right?
I started it at Houston, Texas, before Illinois (inaudible).
: (Inaudible), you know, the famous sort of tenor (inaudible) on that was originally yours, was it?
: Yes. (Inaudible) with the band, you start (inaudible). Well, how long would he let you play?

Long as I wanted because he kept a-saying 'one more Gates,' and I wore myself out playing it. But it -- see, I didn't disrespect him either. I respected him as my boss, and I don't disrespect people. But when -- you don't get bigger than the people that hire you.
: Well, I mean if you -- you know, one might --
Anytime he tell me to cut, I'm going.
: That's right, because he may be cutting the whole (inaudible) --

I did it the other night, and I don't even work for him anymore, but I respect him for what he's done. He know what he want on that show. It's not my problem, you know, so I don't go in to be the big (inaudible). It's a Lionel Hampton situation. And I wasn't working for Hamp, and Hamp didn't pay me. George Mead's office paid me off. But I respect what I (inaudible) worked for. They told me that in front.
